correctness.rationale: The two pivotal-binomial cases yield exact identity for every m and any latent law. Under the two-atom assumptions s<t, the sign is exactly H-r^(m+1) with strict positive factor; r>1 gives a single switch. Explicit H_j lies strictly between consecutive powers r^j and r^(j+1), while w_j>1/5 forces marginal competence over half. Covariances equal latent variance. Exact moment-matched pair gives identical Bernoulli two-voter law, with n=5 uniquely optimal for one and strict increase for the other. No infinite claim depends on finite calculations. Exact verifier checked 720 gain identities and 1886 finite designed signs.

originality.rationale: The checked results recognize correlated votes and insufficiency of pairwise summaries, but the accessible precise statements do not give the two-environment geometric single-switch law, realize every chosen finite odd optimum with positively correlated competent votes, or exhibit the exact moment-matched monotonicity reversal. The generic pairwise-insufficiency principle is explicitly treated as prior knowledge; publication-wide equivalence risk remains.
residual_risks: A general dependent-jury marginal improvement formula may subsume the elementary gain identity; the claimed contribution relies on the complete two-environment phase classification and constructive separation, not invention of the difference formula.
Full-text coverage of Berend–Sapir (2007) and other papers on finite optimal correlated juries is incomplete; equivalent two-atom statements remain possible.
Results are purely theoretical and assume a common latent environment rather than arbitrary correlation or strategic votes.

value.rationale: Optimal juror count under shared task difficulty is a natural mathematically motivated decision-design question. The phase law supplies an exact global optimum and an explicit arbitrary-size construction despite favorable marginal competence and positive pairwise correlation. The moment-matched pair demonstrates the substantive limitation of pairwise correlation-based group-design judgments; it does not treat generic higher-order insufficiency as original.
